subject: Post-call: EvokeAI integration — SDK auth, routing & observability handshake
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Li <sasha@evokeai.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@evokeai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — EvokeAI integration: SDK auth, routing & observability

Hi Sasha / Tom —

Great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

1) Goal: get Redwood SDK into EvokeAI staging to validate auth flow, structured output (tool-calling), and basic observability hooks (trace IDs, latency headers, a minimal dashboard).
2) Auth: Evoke prefers OIDC client-credentials for server-to-server. We scoped two options: short-lived access tokens issued by Evoke IdP or Redwood-managed signed JWTs with rotation.
3) Routing / models: primary routing rule = latency-priority for US region; fallback to quantized Llama-variant when under heavy load or to control cost.
4) Structured output: Evoke will use Redwood function-calling for product metadata enrichment. We proposed function schema and will send a small example payload.
5) Embeddings / reranker: Evoke will start with embeddings for retrieval + a lightweight neural reranker (top-10 candidates) if latency remains acceptable.
6) Observability: key asks from Evoke: inject trace IDs (they prefer x-evoke-trace or x-request-id), send latency breakdown headers (x-redwood-latency: serve=model=XX;model=YY;cache=ZZ), and expose per-request token counts in logs.

Attachments: architecture diagram (evoke-sdk-arch.png). Live brief: https://drive.google.com/evoke-integration-brief

Proposed immediate next steps (owners):
- Dev: sketch SDK changes & sample curl snippets for OIDC flow (Dev) — target 2027-02-18
- Marissa: assemble legal/scoping items + HubSpot deal (Marissa) — target 2027-02-19
- Evoke: confirm log ingestion endpoint and retention requirements (Sasha/Tom) — target 2027-02-17

Can you confirm the retention (logs/telemetry), and whether you need any on-prem/VPC options for audit before staging?

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — EvokeAI integration: SDK auth, routing & observability

Thanks Hannah — this looks good. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: we prefer 90 days of indexing for logs/trace events in Splunk; longer cold storage is fine but not required for initial integration.
- Trace header: our infra currently prefers x-evoke-trace for cross-service stitching; we can accept x-request-id as fallback.
- Latency header content: if possible, send a single header we can parse: x-redwood-latency: serve=22;model=18;cache=4. We’ll map those values to our dashboard.
- Embeddings vs reranker: we want to start with embedding-based retrieval (dense) and run a small neural reranker on top. Top-10 candidates and no more than ~200ms additional latency budget for reranking.

We can confirm the IdP OIDC details this week — I’ll send a service account and metadata by EOD Tuesday (2027-02-16).

Also: for initial staging we don’t need on-prem. We will want to review SOC2 artifacts before production.

— Sasha
Sasha Li
Head of Platform — EvokeAI

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sasha Li <sasha@evokeai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — EvokeAI integration: SDK auth, routing & observability

Adding technical notes + proposal for the SDK/integration surface. Tagged the bits that need Evoke input.

High-level plan (short):
- Auth: implement OIDC client-credentials flow in Redwood SDK core. Flow:
  * Evoke IdP issues short-lived access_token (1–2 hours).
  * SDK exchanges client_id/secret to fetch token, caches in memory and refreshes on expiry.
  * Optional: accept Evoke-signed JWTs via header X-EVOKE-JWT if they prefer push model.

- Routing policy config (example):
  { "routing": { "region": "us", "priority": "latency", "fallback": "llama-q4" } }
  (we will provide declarative rule UI in console, but SDK can accept explicit header x-redwood-route).

- Structured output / function-calling: SDK will include a function-call helper that maps to Redwood’s tool-calling interface. We will ship a schema validator and sample mapping.

- Embeddings / reranker: default flow we suggest: retrieve top-50 via dense embeddings, do a neural rerank top-10. Reranker model should run in the same region to avoid cross-region penalty. We will add a tuning knob in the SDK: rerank_window = 10 (configurable).

- Observability hooks (required):
  * Trace IDs: SDK will accept either x-evoke-trace or x-request-id from caller and propagate to Redwood runtime and put into logs (field: trace_id). If no header provided, SDK will generate X-Request-Id UUID and return it in response header.
  * Response latency header: x-redwood-latency: serve={serve_ms};model={model_ms};cache={cache_ms}. We will also include x-request-tokens for per-request token accounting.
  * Logging fields (structured JSON line logs): {"trace_id":"...","request_id":"...","latencies":{...},"model":"...","model_version":"...","tokens_in":12,"tokens_out":34} — we’ll output to stdout for pipeline ingestion; Evoke can ingest into Splunk.

Open Qs for Evoke:
- Will Splunk accept JSON-line events over HTTP or do you prefer pushing files to an ingestion bucket?
- Confirm acceptable token lifetime (1h vs 2h) and whether rotating secrets through KMS is needed.

Sample artifact attached: sample-curl.sh (minimal OIDC token + request example).

If that aligns, I’ll prototype the SDK changes and a small telemetry dashboard with per-route latency breakdown (target PR by 2027-02-18).

— Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Runtime — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — EvokeAI integration: SDK auth, routing & observability

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick confirmations from infra/legal side:

- Logs: Splunk ingestion endpoint is https://splunk-collector.evokeai.com/hec and we accept JSON events. Retention: 90 days hot, 365 days cold.
- SOC2: we’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence before production sign-off; happy to review your standard docs.
- Canary/rollout: we want a staged rollout: canary in staging -> limited prod (5% traffic) -> full. We expect to run the canary week of Feb 22 and go to limited prod around Mar 8 if all checks pass.

Two asks:
1) Can you add an optional header in the SDK that surfaces model decoding latency separately (x-redwood-latency already discussed) but specifically model_token_decode_ms? Some of our telemetry uses model_token_decode for tokenization profiling.
2) For reranker: please expose a debug flag that returns reranker_scores in the response body when enabled (masked in prod unless requested).

We’ll send the OIDC metadata tomorrow EOD. If you can share a short SOC2 checklist and the HubSpot deal id (for procurement), that’ll help speed approvals.

— Tom
Tom Reyes
VP Engineering — EvokeAI
